findings.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — "const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);" binds calendar mutation credentials to the requesting attendee or team administrator rather than the booking organizer, so an authorized non-organizer adds database attendees but cannot update the organizer-owned calendar integration (P1, confidence: 100).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — "!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)" checks a stale attendee snapshot before the separate "createMany" write at line 101, so concurrent add-guest mutations for the same email both pass and create duplicate attendees because no database uniqueness invariant arbitrates the race (P1, confidence: 100).

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:529 — `emailsToSend.push(sendEmail(() => new OrganizerAddGuestsEmail({ calEvent: calendarEvent })));` sends host and team notifications even when the event type’s `disableStandardEmails.all.host` preference is enabled, so hosts who opted out receive an unsolicited guest-change email (P1, confidence: 100).

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:539 — `emailsToSend.push(...calendarEvent.attendees.map((attendee) => {` sends both the new-invite and existing-attendee messages without checking `disableStandardEmails.all.attendee`, so attendees who opted out receive guest-change notifications (P1, confidence: 100).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — `const uniqueGuests = guests.filter((guest) => !booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email) && !blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest));` treats email addresses as case-sensitive, so adding `ALICE@example.com` to a booking already containing `alice@example.com` creates a duplicate attendee and sends duplicate calendar invitations (P2, confidence: 100).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — `const uniqueGuests = guests.filter((guest) => !booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email) && !blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest));` never removes duplicate values within `guests`, so a direct mutation with the same valid new address twice inserts and invites that guest twice (P2, confidence: 75).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:77 — `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` compares a lowercased blacklist with the caller’s unnormalized address, so `Blocked@Example.com` bypasses a `blocked@example.com` blacklist entry and is added to the booking (P1, confidence: 100).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:167 — `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` converts an email-rendering or delivery failure into `{ message: "Guests added" }`, so organizers and attendees receive a success response while their required guest-update notifications are silently dropped (P1, confidence: 100).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` compares the unnormalized request email against a lowercased blacklist, so submitting `Blocked@Example.com` bypasses `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS=blocked@example.com` and sends that prohibited recipient a calendar invitation (P1, confidence: 100).

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — "const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);" binds calendar mutation credentials to the requesting attendee or team administrator rather than the booking organizer, so an authorized non-organizer adds database attendees but cannot update the organizer-owned calendar integration (P1, confidence: 100).

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` gets credentials for the requesting user (ctx.user - who could be an attendee or team admin), not the booking organizer. Looking at the code flow: the handler allows attendees and team admins to add guests (lines 47-51 check isTeamAdminOrOwner, isOrganizer, isAttendee), but then uses ctx.user's credentials for the EventManager to update calendar attendees. This means when a non-organizer (attendee or team admin) adds guests, the calendar update will use their credentials instead of the organizer's, which would fail to update the organizer's calendar integration. The booking.user with credentials is fetched but not used for the EventManager.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — "!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)" checks a stale attendee snapshot before the separate "createMany" write at line 101, so concurrent add-guest mutations for the same email both pass and create duplicate attendees because no database uniqueness invariant arbitrates the race (P1, confidence: 100).

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a race condition in addGuests.handler.ts. At line 74, the code filters guests against booking.attendees (fetched at line 27-42), then at line 85-101 creates new attendees with createMany. There's no database-level uniqueness constraint or transaction to prevent concurrent requests from both passing the check and creating duplicate attendees for the same email. The diff shows no unique constraint on the attendees table for (bookingId, email) combination, making this a valid TOCTOU race condition.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — `const uniqueGuests = guests.filter((guest) => !booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email) && !blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest));` treats email addresses as case-sensitive, so adding `ALICE@example.com` to a booking already containing `alice@example.com` creates a duplicate attendee and sends duplicate calendar invitations (P2, confidence: 100).

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `uniqueGuests` is filtered using direct string comparison `guest === attendee.email` without any case normalization. Email addresses are case-insensitive per RFC 5321, so 'ALICE@example.com' and 'alice@example.com' should be treated as the same address. The code would allow adding 'ALICE@example.com' when 'alice@example.com' already exists, creating duplicate attendees. The blacklist check also uses case-sensitive comparison via `includes()`. This is a real bug that could cause duplicate calendar invitations.
